subject: melanopsin/ipRGC spatial vision
claim: Selective melanopsin modulation in humans can alter spatial contrast sensitivity, supporting a role for melanopsin beyond circadian and pupillary functions.
mechanism: melanopsin-driven retinal signaling contributing to brightness/contrast pathways
limitations: The contribution of melanopsin to color appearance remains debated and task-dependent.
contradictions: Melanopsin effects on color are less settled than effects on brightness/contrast.

sources.title: Enhanced human contrast sensitivity with increased stimulation of melanopsin in intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells
sources.authors: Sung-En Chien; Su-Ling Yeh; Wakayo Yamashita; Sei-Ichi Tsujimura

subject: LSD, 5-HT2A and visual perception
claim: Low-dose LSD altered subjective visual qualities such as saturation, blur and visual dynamics, while contextual contrast suppression was not measurably changed in a small crossover study; ketanserin evidence supports a broader 5-HT2A contribution to psychedelic visual effects.
limitations: Small sample and task-specific null result; subjective and psychophysical measures may dissociate.
contradictions: Subjective visual change did not imply a measurable change in contextual contrast suppression in this study.

sources.title: Low-dose lysergic acid diethylamide alters subjective visual perception but not visual contrast surround suppression
sources.authors: Lucca F Jaeckel; Deborah Logvinski; Mika Kanana; Felix Müller; Nicolai Rohner; Anna M Becker; Matthias E Liechti; Philipp Sterzer

subject: ethambutol ocular toxicity
claim: Ethambutol exposure can produce subclinical structural and electrophysiological retinal/optic changes before standard behavioral deficits are evident.
mechanism: toxic injury affecting retinal ganglion-cell/optic pathways with electrophysiological delay
limitations: Color findings vary across studies and structural/electrophysiological abnormalities are not equivalent to clinical visual loss.
contradictions: Color-vision findings are inconsistent across cohorts.

sources.title: Prospective study to evaluate incidence and indicators for early detection of ethambutol toxicity
sources.authors: Sohini Mandal; Rohit Saxena; Rebika Dhiman; Anant Mohan; Srikanta Kumar Padhy; Swati Phuljhele; Pradeep Sharma; Randeep Guleria

subject: two-photon infrared perception
claim: Human photopigments can support visible perception through simultaneous two-photon absorption of infrared light; recent work demonstrated infrared color mixing including white and multiple hues.
mechanism: nonlinear two-photon absorption by visual photopigments
limitations: This is nonlinear two-photon perception, not ordinary infrared vision, and requires specialized optical conditions.

sources.authors: Pedro Gil; Juan Tabernero; Silvestre Manzanera; Christina Schwarz; Pablo Artal

sources.authors: Hannah K Doyle; Sarah R Herbeck; Avery E Boehm; Jacob E Vanston; Ren Ng; William S Tuten; Austin Roorda

subject: Substance P/dopamine retinal gain in zebrafish
claim: Substance P and dopamine participate in antagonistic circadian control of retinal contrast gain in zebrafish; Substance P reduced contrast sensitivity most strongly in transient high-frequency ON/OFF channels.
mechanism: neuromodulatory control of retinal gain across circadian state
limitations: Animal model; magnitude and channel organization should not be assumed to transfer directly to humans.

sources.title: Substance P and dopamine form a "push-pull" system that diurnally regulates retinal gain
sources.authors: José Moya-Díaz; Patrício Simões; Leon Lagnado

subject: visual snow and motion processing
claim: Visual snow can interact strongly with motion adaptation: most participants in one small study reported visual-snow motion opposite to an adapting grating, while several basic visual measures remained normal.
mechanism: interaction between persistent visual-noise percepts and motion-adaptation processing
limitations: Very small sample; network-level 7T findings and psychophysical dissociations do not establish a single causal mechanism.
contradictions: Normal performance on several basic visual measures argues against a simple global hyperexcitability account.
